newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds end firm amid U.S. gains-eye on FOMC.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds end firm amid U.S. gains-eye on FOMC.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed slightly firmer in quiet trade on Monday, boosted by gains in U.S. Treasuries, with both markets focused on Tuesday's meeting of the Federal Reserve's rate-setting committee, analysts said.

"Toward the afternoon, right while things were at their dullest, we saw some decent buying in the U.S. market, which caused dealers in Canada to scramble and mark prices up," said Jeoff Hall, Canadian market analyst with Technical Data.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.20 at C$101.80 to yield 7.837 percent against the U.S. 30-year benchmark, which rose 10/32 to yield 7.02 percent.
